newsitem.title: ITALY: Berisha children flee Albania on ferry to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Berisha children flee Albania on ferry to Italy.

text.p: Two children of Albanian President Sali Berisha fled the troubled Balkan country to Italy on Thursday with armed bodyguards, an official for the shipping line which brought them across the Adriatic said.
Domenica Stea said Berisha's children, a man and a woman he thought were in their twenties, had diplomatic passports and had been accompanied on board the Italian ferry Palladio by five armed guards.

"They were young and they looked a bit worried," Stea told Reuters by telephone from the southern port of Bari, where the ferry docked with 77 passengers after a voyage from the Albanian port of Durres.
Stea, agent in Bari for the ship's owner Adriatica, was unable to give the childrens' first names but said he had seen them on board and read their surnames on the passenger list.
The Italian news agency AGI, reporting from Bari, named them as Argita Berisha and her brother Sokul.
It said they boarded a white minibus after disembarking and were driven from the port under a heavy police escort. Police in Bari would not immediately confirm details.
Albania plunged deeper into anarchy on Thursday as armed unrest sparked by popular anger at the collapse of shady savings scheme spread to the impoverished state's capital Tirana.
Insurgents who have seized most of the south of the country after raiding state armouries have refused to lay down their arms until Berisha resigns.
Stea said the five guards had handed their weapons over to the Palladio's captain after the party boarded the ferry.

They and 11 other Albanians without Italian visas or proper documents were detained on board in Bari after the other passengers, including Italians, Belgians, Danes and Albanians, disembarked, Stea said.
Police were out in force in Bari port when the ship arrived and boarded her to question passengers and examine documents.
The Palladio and other vessels in Durres port on Thursday had to make a hasty departure after crowds of Albanians, reported to be armed with stones, stormed into the docks.
Some 40 Albanians managed to rush aboard another merchant vessel which was heading under naval escort late on Thursday for the Italian port of Brindisi.
A third ship, the Italian ferry Annamaria Lauro, reached the port of Otranto on Thursday with just eight passengers after having to leave Durres hours ahead of schedule, Italian coastguards said.
